clue.text: See 10
The team sledger and rattler?

parts.note: a side is a team, as in cricket or football
in cricket a sledger taunts the batsman, someone who winds him up, so a winder

explanation.surface: A cricket team's chief sledger rattles the opposition with insults.
explanation.walkthrough: Sledging is the cricket habit of insulting batsmen to unsettle them. 'rattler' looks like someone who rattles opponents, but it is a rattlesnake; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidewinder is a small North American rattlesnake that moves sideways across sand.

clue.text: Checked the others fell

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remainder
rain fell, so fell can mean rained

explanation.surface: Someone stopped short while the rest of the group fell down.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked in the sense of held back or curbed is a synonym of restrained.

clue.text: Poet awoke at Shelley's house

indicators.note: the words awoke at Shelley's house, or contain, the letters of the poet in an unbroken run

explanation.surface: A poet wakes up while staying at Shelley's home.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, a friend of Shelley.

clue.text: Do up sacrifice where one's accepted responsibility for drop in cover price

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for do is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them

indicators.note: the sacrifice word takes in the letter for one, accepting it inside

parts.note: a lamb is the classic sacrificial animal
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for is
onus means responsibility or burden

explanation.surface: A garbled insurance tale of someone owning up to blame, which cuts their policy cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do up' looks like fastening something, but 'up' reverses the swindle word in this down clue. A no-claim bonus is the discount an insurer gives for a year without claims.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer cuts the premium for a policyholder who has made no claim, a reduction in the price of cover.

clue.text: Activate footrest right away

indicators.note: right is taken away from the footrest word

parts.note: a stirrup is the rider's footrest on a saddle

explanation.surface: Someone sets a footrest working, then shifts it out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up something is to rouse it into action, a synonym of activate.

clue.text: Three-point turn of obscenity, catching fish

indicators.note: the turned word for obscenity catches the fishing word inside it
turn of means the word for obscenity is turned round

parts.note: dirt is smut or obscenity
to fish is to angle

explanation.surface: A driver doing a three-point turn swears while a fish is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-point turn' reads as one driving phrase, but the definition stops at 'Three-point'; 'turn of' gives TRID, which 'catching' wraps round the fishing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangled means formed into a triangle, a shape with three points.

clue.text: Demon — that's a surprise! — making an appearance in Rugby

indicators.note: the exclamation turns up inside the abbreviation for Rugby

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A demon unexpectedly appears in a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: Rahu is a demon in Hindu myth who swallows the sun or moon to cause eclipses.

clue.text: See 26
See10
Approaching picket line?

parts.note: a picket line is made up of workers on strike, so walking up to one puts you close to those who strike, a phrase that also means nearly in reach

explanation.surface: Someone walks up towards a line of workers picketing outside a factory gate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for being close enough to reach or attack something, so it means approaching.

clue.text: Belief of those that freeze food in small packages, as Swift saw it

indicators.note: the belief belongs to the frozen-food company, so its name comes first

parts.words: those that freeze food in small packages
parts.note: Birds Eye is a British brand of frozen food, sold in packs
a view is an opinion or belief

explanation.surface: Jonathan Swift's opinion of the firm that sells packets of frozen food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like the satirist Jonathan Swift, but it is the bird, which sees from high above.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's-eye view is the view from above, as a swift flying overhead would see the ground.

clue.text: Here operative comes together with French actor in business

parts.note: a works is a factory or business
Jacques Tati was a French actor and film-maker
on and in both mean present or operating, as with a light

explanation.surface: An agent arrives with a French actor to work in a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operative' looks like a secret agent; here it is a worker, and the workstation is where one sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A workstation is the desk or place where an operator does their job, so it is where an operative is.

clue.text: Boy of 13's left arm's replaced in air raid at Virginia hospital

indicators.note: the letter for left is replaced by the word arm in the air raid word

parts.note: a blitz is an intense air raid
taken as written, arm
VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A thirteen-year-old's injured arm is replaced in a Virginia hospital after an air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' swaps the L in BLITZ for ARM, giving BARMITZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar mitzvah is a Jewish boy who comes of religious age at thirteen, as well as the ceremony.

clue.text: Tightly-held Latvian acting without control

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian
something held tightly is in a firm grip

explanation.surface: A Latvian performer clings tightly on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting rip is an idiom for acting freely and without restraint.

clue.text: Cry from Yard close by, seizing drug

indicators.note: the word for close by grabs the drug letter inside

parts.note: nigh means near or close by
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Police from Scotland Yard grab drugs nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' looks like Scotland Yard, but in horse racing a trainer's yard is the stable, so the cry is a horse's.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the call a horse gives, the sort heard in a racing stable.

clue.text: Kind of car to develop second

parts.note: to hatch a plan is to develop it
to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: Instructions to develop an idea and then support it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchback is a car body with a rear door that opens upwards.

clue.text: Does this extend from the 5th to 15th centuries?

definitions.text: Does this extend from the 5th to 15th centuries?

parts.words: Does this extend from the 5th to 15th centuries?
parts.note: the ... ran from about the fifth to the fifteenth century; really it is the thickening waist of later life

explanation.surface: A history question about the span of the medieval period.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the weight people put on round the waist in their forties and fifties, punned as the extent of the medieval era.

clue.text: Chosen ones perhaps availed themselves of bus conductor

parts.note: the elect are those chosen, as by God
people who used a bus rode on it

explanation.surface: The chosen few took the bus and spoke to its conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' looks like the bus conductor, but it is an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a metal conductor through which current enters or leaves a circuit.

clue.text: Dismiss, having kept the enemy back

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: time is called the enemy, so to keep it is to have timed something

explanation.surface: An officer sacks someone after they had held off the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TIMED. Time is called 'the enemy' in the saying 'time is the enemy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Demit is an old word meaning to dismiss or to resign from an office.

clue.text: With difficulty, a nurse gets him to swallow

indicators.note: something done with difficulty is awkward and struggles, so the letters are worked around

explanation.surface: A nurse struggles to get a patient to swallow his pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With difficulty' rearranges A NURSE HIM TO. 'swallow' looks like a verb about pills; it is the bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: The house martin is a small bird of the swallow family that nests under eaves.

clue.text: Is this lion on the slope? Just about

indicators.note: just about means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: aslant means slanting or on a slope

explanation.surface: A question whether a lion on a hillside counts as nearly on the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just about' cuts the T from ASLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslan is the great lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia books.

clue.text: Goddess is living in the second boat from Oxford

definitions.meaning: the Egyptian goddess of motherhood and magic
Oxford University's reserve crew in the Boat Race rows under the name of the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: A goddess is said to live aboard Oxford's reserve rowing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Isis is the Oxford reserve eight, named after the Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one name: the Egyptian deity and the Oxford reserve boat named after the river.

clue.text: A killer from Pomona, say, half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut means the word loses its second half

parts.note: Pomona is the old name of Mainland, the largest Orkney island, so someone from there is an Orcadian

explanation.surface: A drunken killer from the Californian town of Pomona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' (British slang for drunk) here cuts ORCADIAN in half. Pomona looks like the Californian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is the killer whale, a predator of seals and fish.

clue.text: See 17
On the evidence of her dietary preferences, she should be a regular broadcaster

definitions.text: On the evidence of her dietary preferences, she should be a regular broadcaster

parts.words: On the evidence of her dietary preferences, she should be a regular broadcaster
parts.note: a woman fond of figs, a laxative fruit, should be regular; the name read as two words is a BBC radio presenter

explanation.surface: Someone guesses from a woman's diet that she must be regular.
explanation.walkthrough: Fi Glover is a BBC radio presenter; split differently her name says she loves figs, which keep the bowels regular.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio broadcaster's name read as one phrase describes a woman who loves figs, hence regular.

clue.text: Shaft's £25 — and I'm walking on it!

parts.note: a shank is a shaft, as of a tool or a leg
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: Someone boasts their walking stick cost twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: To go on shanks's pony is British slang for going on foot, using your own legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one's own legs as transport, so it is what a walker travels on.

clue.text: Pairing's tense, but comes out on top with it

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
someone who comes out on top wins
it, meaning the latest fashion, is what is hip

explanation.surface: A tense couple who end up winning with style.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinship is the state of being twins, a close pairing.
